neighbours.label: ' whether' opening a concessive 'whether X or Y / or not' clause after a comma (regardless-of sense)
fire: The bus runs every morning, whether there are passengers or not.
She practises the violin daily, whether she feels like it or not.
The rules apply to everyone, whether rich or poor.
He wears the same coat all year, whether it is hot or cold.
The shop stays open on holidays, whether customers come or not.
Our dog wants a walk at six, whether it rains or shines.
You will be paid the same, whether you work from home or the office.
The festival goes ahead every year, whether the town likes it or not.
quiet: The bus runs every morning, even when there are no passengers.
She practises the violin daily, though she rarely feels like it.
The rules apply to everyone, rich and poor alike.
He wears the same coat all year, hot weather and cold.
The shop stays open on holidays, and customers usually come.
Our dog wants a walk at six, rain or shine.
You will be paid the same, no matter where you work.
The festival goes ahead every year, regardless of the town's opinion.

notes: Card: ' whether' 29/32 top peaks, mostly after a comma. Probe: concessive 0.90/0.73, embedded question 'wonder whether' 0.27, ' if' up to 0.45 so near misses avoid 'if'.
